BiblicalUsage: Pidyom is a ransom, the price paid to redeem a life. A man whose ox killed another could give the ransom of his life in Exodus 21:30, and Moses took redemption money for the firstborn over the number of the Levites in Numbers 3:49. But Psalms 49:8 says the redemption of a soul is precious, and it ceases forever — no man's money can buy it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the ransom of a soul was too costly for any man to pay, which is why God paid it Himself. That is the whole gospel hidden in one word.
